description: Backend half of auth for an Express (Node) API: verifies Firebase ID tokens and serves the auth contract (GET /api/auth/me, POST /api/auth/register). Pair it with any frontend that follows contracts/auth.
provides: setupAuth(app): one call that loads credentials, optionally adds CORS, and mounts /api/auth/me and /api/auth/register
onRegister hook for saving new users in your own database
Works in CommonJS and ES-module projects (the module folder pins itself to CommonJS)

backend: Put your Firebase service-account key at the path set in .env (GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS).
Add .env and the key file to .gitignore.
Protect your own routes: app.get('/api/things', requireAuth, (req, res) => res.json({ uid: req.user.uid }))

prompts.ask: Where does your frontend run in development (for backend CORS)?

manual: In your Express app, right after it is created:
const { setupAuth, requireAuth } = require('./auth_module')   // or: import { setupAuth, requireAuth } from './auth_module/index.js'
setupAuth(app, { corsOrigins: ['{{frontendOrigin}}'] })       // drop corsOrigins if you already use the cors package
app.get('/api/things', requireAuth, (req, res) => res.json({ uid: req.user.uid }))
